title: Batch vs Streaming
interviewAnswer: Batch processing handles bounded datasets on a schedule; streaming processes events continuously or in small increments. Choose based on freshness requirements, complexity, cost and correctness needs.
why: Batch vs streaming is a core architecture trade-off for data and ML systems: freshness, complexity, cost and correctness all change.
intuition: Batch waits and processes a bounded collection. Streaming processes an unbounded flow continuously or in small micro-batches.
deepDive: Batch is simpler, cheaper and easier to reproduce when minute/hour/day freshness is sufficient. Streaming is justified when decisions need low event-to-action latency. Stream processing introduces ordering, event time, late data, state, checkpoints and delivery semantics. Many systems combine a streaming serving path with batch recomputation/backfills.
workedExample: Daily model-feature recomputation is naturally batch. Fraud detection at payment time requires streaming/online features because waiting until tomorrow is useless.
commonMistakes: Choosing streaming because it sounds modern without a latency requirement.
Confusing Kafka ingestion with stream processing.
Ignoring late/out-of-order events and state recovery.
followUps: What is the operational cost of streaming?
production: Define freshness SLOs first. Use the simplest architecture that meets them, and design replay/backfill paths so real-time state can be recovered after bugs or outages.
